measurement_metadata.methodology: chars/4 token approximation. Old costs from B2-Alpha baseline or measured. New costs measured from actual tool output.

benchmarks.name: Read: Full KB entry vs smart_read selective fields
benchmarks.notes: Old: read full KB-0008.md (3778 chars). New: smart_read returns only title+tags+summary (450 chars). Tool self-reports 89% savings.

benchmarks.name: Read: Full KB entry vs query_kb read selective fields
benchmarks.notes: query_kb returns even more compact output (399 chars) with truncated summary. Slightly better than smart_read.

benchmarks.name: Search: Full index.json read vs smart_search
benchmarks.notes: Old: read entire index.json (24373 chars) to find database entries. New: smart_search returns 5 results with context snippets (1251 chars). Massive savings.

benchmarks.name: Search: Full index.json read vs query_kb search
benchmarks.notes: query_kb search is even more compact (491 chars), returning tabular output with 1 result (fewer matches but more token-efficient). Best search result.

benchmarks.name: List/browse: Full index.json vs query_kb summary
benchmarks.notes: Summary provides high-level counts and categories per resource type (838 chars). Perfect for 'what exists?' queries.

benchmarks.name: List/browse: Full index.json vs query_kb list CSV
benchmarks.notes: CSV list of all 31 KB entries with id,title,category,date (2897 chars). Good for browsing all entries without full metadata.

benchmarks.name: List/browse: Full index.json vs SUMMARY.json (Level 0)
benchmarks.notes: SUMMARY.json is 317 chars containing just entry count, categories, id range, and last_updated. Minimal Level 0 overview.

benchmarks.name: List/browse: Full index.json vs INDEX_COMPACT.json (Level 1)
benchmarks.notes: INDEX_COMPACT.json is 6364 chars. Moderate savings -- still has per-entry data but in compact format.

benchmarks.name: Write: Template+content+index cycle vs smart_write dry-run
benchmarks.command: echo 'content' | python3 storage/scripts/smart_write.py --type kb --title 'Benchmark Test Entry' --category testing --tags benchmark,test --dry-run
benchmarks.notes: Old: read template (146 tokens) + write content (2079 tokens) + read index (6168 tokens) + rewrite index (6168 tokens) = 14561. New: smart_write handles all internally, agent only sees 641 chars of confirmation. Biggest savings of all benchmarks.

benchmarks.name: Tags: Full index.json parse vs query_kb tags
benchmarks.notes: Returns all tags with usage counts (5670 chars). Large output because there are 130+ unique tags. Still 77% savings vs reading full index.

benchmarks.name: Relationships: Full index.json parse vs query_kb related
benchmarks.notes: Returns builds-on chain (ancestors+children) and shared-tag matches (2724 chars). Rich relationship data without reading the full index.

edge_cases.test: CSV output saves tokens vs JSON
edge_cases.result: CSV: 2897 chars (724 tokens). JSON: 5283 chars (1321 tokens). CSV is 45.2% smaller. Confirmed: CSV format saves significant tokens.
Returns clear error: 'Error: Entry KB-9999 not found.' with exit code 1

bugs_found: smart_search --max-tokens 50 returns 0 results with no warning. A very low token budget silently produces empty output instead of warning the user or showing at least one truncated result.
query_kb search for 'database' only returns 1 result (KB-0008) despite --limit 5, while smart_search finds 5 relevant entries. query_kb may use stricter matching or different scoring.
usability_issues: smart_read and query_kb read have slightly different output formats. smart_read includes the full summary text while query_kb truncates it. No obvious way to control truncation length in query_kb.
query_kb tags output for KB type returns 130+ tags (5670 chars). For large tag sets this is still expensive. Could benefit from a --limit or --min-count filter.
INDEX_COMPACT.json at 6364 chars provides only 73.9% reduction -- it could be further compressed by removing redundant fields.
recommendations: Add --min-count flag to query_kb tags to filter low-frequency tags (would reduce 5670 chars to ~500 chars for tags with count >= 2)
Fix smart_search --max-tokens to always return at least 1 result or emit a warning when budget is insufficient
Investigate query_kb search scoring -- it finds fewer results than smart_search for the same query. Consider aligning algorithms.
Add --truncate-length option to query_kb read for controlling summary length
Consider compressing INDEX_COMPACT.json further -- current savings (73.9%) lag behind other tools (88-99%)
CSV format should be the default for list operations -- it saves 45% vs JSON with no loss of essential information

summary.headline_metric: 90.2% average token reduction across all 11 benchmarks (11.7x overall speedup)
summary.best_improvement: Write operations: 98.9% reduction (91x speedup) via smart_write handling template+index internally
summary.worst_improvement: INDEX_COMPACT.json: 73.9% reduction (3.8x speedup) -- still contains per-entry data in compact form
summary.details: All tools handle errors gracefully with clear messages and proper exit codes. Two minor bugs found: (1) smart_search --max-tokens with very low budgets returns empty results silently, (2) query_kb search finds fewer results than smart_search for the same query. Neither bug is blocking. CSV output saves 45% over JSON for list operations. The tiered approach (SUMMARY.json at 79 tokens -> query_kb summary at 210 tokens -> query_kb list at 724 tokens -> full index at 6093 tokens) provides excellent progressive disclosure. Overall assessment: production-ready with minor improvements recommended.
